[h1][i]«Выйти без наушников из дома — то же самое, что выйти в космос без кислорода»[/i][/h1]

Эй, привет, космические искатели! Вы не поверите, что со мной произошло в игре Cosmophony! Это как если бы кто-то смешал симфонию и космос, и я, такой весь важный, оказался в центре этой музыкально-звёздной пучины! Сначала, значит, я думал, что попал в пришельческое выступление на танцовщиц с Венеры, но на деле — я не просто слушатель, я здесь главный дирижёр!

Игра начинается, и что я вижу? Я стал космическим героем, который должен собирать звуки, как будто они — счастливые покемоны, разбежавшиеся везде по галактике. Надавил на кнопку, и — дак-док-док! Музыка началась, как будто мой космический авиатор вдруг решил, что у нас сегодня рок-концерт! Звуки виляют, скачут, и я бегаю по платформам, как будто спонтанно забыл, где на самом деле находятся мои ноги. Всё дело в том, что мне надо укрощать эти звуковые волны и направлять их в нужный ритм, чтобы пройти на следующий уровень. Сложность-то, знаете ли, в том, что эти звуки такие шаловливые, как котята – бегают, путаются под ногами и постоянно разыгрывают шутки!

Графика в Cosmophony просто космическая — настолько яркая и красочная, что я даже начал задумываться, не злюсь ли я на свои обычные серые тапки. Я прямо перед экраном, как будто пытаюсь достучаться до этих звуков — «Эй, мелодии! Куда вы убегаете?!». И эта зажигательная музыка – она будто заставляет тебя танцевать, даже когда ты всего лишь сидишь на диване, заедая чипсы и надеясь, что родители не зайдут!

А сложность игры — о, это настоящий экшн! Иногда я просто чувствовал себя как киборг на вечеринке на дискотеке, где вместо того, чтобы просто танцевать, мне надо ещё и комбинировать эти звуки с правильными движениями! Я в каждом уровне будто делаю «Супермен» с двумя левыми ногами, пытаясь угадать, в какую сторону прыгнуть. При этом смеюсь сам над собой, потому что порой попадаю в ноты не то что бы не туда – это вообще участник самого крутого отделения в конкурсе «Непопадание в ноты года».

Короче говоря, если вы хотите провести время за игрой, где сразу и музыка, и бит, и ваша жизнь превращается в экшен-музыку с задором, Cosmophony — это то, что вам нужно! Стремитесь к своей космической симфонии, ловите звуки и не забывайте — немножко веселья никогда не помешает! Так что, запускайте игру и готовьтесь танцевать вместе с звёздами!

7 космопиу из 10

[h1] Category: Unbearable Games [/h1]

Sorry, but I’m seriously running out of ideas for previews because there are some types of games that you just can’t beat no matter how hard you try.

This rhythm game can easily be called one of the hardest out there, and the worst part is, its difficulty isn’t fun at all—it’s just draining. There are only five levels, and you control something that, in its minimalism, kind of looks like a spaceship. To the music of DJ Salaryman, you have to move across just six lanes, avoid crashing into blocks, and destroy triangles along the way that are annoying but don’t actually attack you. And that’s it—until the level ends. Sounds simple, but in reality, it’s pure hell.

There are some positives here, but they're so minor that they hardly save things.  

You can at least recognize the originality of the concept. Even though the plot sort of revolves around some cosmic mega-being that messed up and picked us to be killed, not everyone would dare to justify what’s happening, even in a ridiculous way.  

There’s also a chance for practice. Even though each level can give a maximum of four stars (split between the two modes and their conditions), it doesn’t really affect progression. Besides the star for completing a level, you can snag another one by destroying all the triangles. But honestly, who cares about that if moving forward only depends on finishing the main mode?  

And yeah, since we started with the downsides, let’s kick off a bit off-track. Destroying triangles feels less like part of the core gameplay and more like a completely unnecessary, tacked-on feature.

Now for the main thing: pure psychedelia, and not a fun kind at all. The developer decided to shove some totally out-of-place stock videos into the background of each level, which, combined with the music, feels completely off. Because of this, it feels like you’ve stumbled into a druggie party rather than a music rhythm game. As for the overly saturated colors—ugh, it’s just a total eyesore when it all comes together.

The music and sounds are another torture. The tracks themselves are brain-melting (personally, I can’t stand drum and bass, and here it’s at its worst), the game volume is way too high and grating. Moving the ship often doesn’t match the beats, and neither do the shots to destroy the triangles, which is just unforgivable in a rhythm game.

Too hard. The controls are clunky, and the 60 Hz lock doesn't make things any better. The obstacles and blocks are just thrown around haphazardly; moving between them on the fourth level is basically impossible. And I won't even get started on the sudden, basically random speed boosts in the music (it’s part of the gameplay, not a bug).  

No Steam Cloud means, as other players complain in their reviews, that if you delete the game, you have to start over from scratch. That pretty much kills any desire to come back to it. Also, there's no Steam Workshop—even though the game hints that you can load your own music, it either doesn’t actually work or the developers couldn’t be bothered to explain how.

I couldn’t get past the fourth level. Honestly, if the game worked like Geometry Dash, where almost all levels are unlocked from the start (even for practice, and by the way – you get rewarded for completing them in that mode, even better), I’d at least have been able to enjoy the content here fully. But since the developer is basically mocking the players, I have zero interest in showing any loyalty to this game.

This game is only good for earning Steam cards and achievements. Other than that, it’s completely unplayable. Don’t waste your time and nerves on it.

Si vous recherchez un jeu de rythme et d'adresse court mais bien corsé, je vous recommande sans hésitation Cosmophony ! 

Sa DA minimaliste et son OST drum'n'bass marchent très bien ensemble, et même si le jeu n'a que 5 niveaux, croyez-moi vous allez sentir le gap de difficulté plus le jeu avance. Les deux premiers niveaux sont faciles et se finissent vite, mais c'est dès le troisième et surtout pour les deux derniers qu'on comprend pleinement qu'en vérité, Cosmophony est aussi un jeu de mémoire !
Les patterns arrivent à une vitesse de fou furieux et il vous faudra non seulement une mémoire musculaire (ainsi qu'une bonne endurance des doigts) mais aussi des post-its mentaux pour apprendre de vos erreurs et vous souvenir de petites astuces qui seront vitales pour compléter chaque challenge. Ainsi, les moments où je comprenais un détail aidant fortement la progression étaient très satisfaisants.
Malgré tout, même si les hitboxs sont souvent très bien réglées, il y a, vitesse démentielle oblige, pas mal de moments où vous aurez l'impression que le jeu décide de vous tuer purement et simplement, sans que ce soit visuellement de votre faute. Armez-vous de patience donc, car l'ultime niveau 5 est assez brutal mais toutefois très bien pensé dans ses patterns.

Chipotage, mais les rares passages avec du texte comportent régulièrement des fautes de français comme "s'il te plais" ; ça la fout un peu mal, on dirait que les devs ne se sont pas relus.

Recommended for those who like a challenge and electronic music.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

**Cosmophony İncelemesi: Müziğin Ritmiyle Dolu Bir Deneyim**

Cosmophony, müzikle yoğrulmuş bir nişancı oyunu olarak, gerçek ve etkileyici bir deneyim arayan oyuncular için özel olarak tasarlanmıştır. Bu oyun, 9 Temmuz 2015 tarihinde Bento-Studio tarafından geliştirilmiş ve Frogames tarafından yayınlanmıştır. İncelemelerde genel bir memnuniyet hakim, çoğunluğu çok olumlu (80) puan almıştır.

Oyuncular, ölmekte olan bir kainatta harap bir tanrıçanın kaderini tamamlaması için onun kalbini kontrol etmekle görevlendirilmiştir. Oyunun amacı, DJ Salaryman tarafından özel olarak oluşturulmuş %100 davul ve basa sahip, canlandırıcı sesleri içeren bir dizi seviye boyunca ilerlemektir.

Cosmophony'nin en dikkat çekici özelliklerinden biri, her zaman 60 FPS hızında akıcı bir oyun deneyimi sunmasıdır. Müziğe dayalı sinestezik tasarımı, oyunculara benzersiz ve tatmin edici bir deneyim vadeder. Psikedelik arka plan videoları, etkileyici HD grafiklerle birleşerek oyuncuları farklı bir dünyaya taşır.

Oyun, özellikle DJ Salaryman tarafından oluşturulan %100 orijinal drum and bass (DnB) sesleri ile zenginleştirilmiştir. Bu sesler, oyunculara oyunun ritmiyle bütünleşmiş bir atmosfer sunar. Ayrıca, oyun merkezi ve iCloud gibi özelliklerle desteklenen Cosmophony, oyun kontrol cihazlarıyla da uyumludur.

Ancak, Cosmophony'nin deneyimli oyunculara yönelik olduğu unutulmamalıdır. Zorluk seviyesi, ilerledikçe artmakta ve oyuncuları meydan okumaya teşvik etmektedir. Bu nedenle, oyuncuların oyunun hızlı tempolu doğasına ayak uydurabilmeleri için biraz tecrübeye sahip olmaları önerilir.

Cosmophony, müzikle nişancı türünü bir araya getirerek oyunculara benzersiz ve çarpıcı bir oyun deneyimi sunuyor. Eğer yoğun bir müzikal deneyim arıyorsanız, Cosmophony sizi etkileyici bir yolculuğa çıkarmaya hazır.

Cosmophony is a mobile app that's been dumped on Steam as if it was a real PC game (it's not)... it's a cash grab from greedy mobile devs.  It's a basic bare bones minimalist/low poly 3-button endless runner, with a lightweight "shooting" element.  Move down an endless tunnel dodging blocks by moving left or right, and sometimes shoot things in your way, all the while listening to completely crap DnB music, some of the worst I've heard, which is inexplicable given how much decent music there is on Creative Commons, the developer could have just asset flipped some of that and the soundtrack would be a lot better. 

Anyway, this is an incredibly shallow mobile app with no value or merit as a serious game for PC gamers.

From a technical perspective, as a mobile app, this doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.

The mobile app features lazy minimalist/untextured low-polygon "retro" assets and visuals, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the early 1990s.  The lack of textures is a method that lazy devs often use to disguise their lack of talent/interest in doing the graphics properly and trying to disguise it under the name of "art", or "We made it look bad on purpose", which really isn't something gamers should have to put up with.  It's unclear why the developers weren't willing to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets and high resolution textures for the mobile app.  It looks bad as a result of their decisions, and that's just another reason to avoid it.

The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the mobile app unplayable for differently-abled gamers, or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts.  

Because this is a mobile app, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the iPhones that the mobile app was designed for.  These are unfortunate handicaps and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was an afterthought for the iPhone developers who are to blame for this.  The mobile app is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for mobile phones forces upon a game.  Once more, mobile devs have made gaming worse for everyone.  I didn't spend thousands on building a gaming rig just so I could pretend it's an iPhone.

These technical defects push this mobile app below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.

In an attempt to excuse the low quality of delivery here, the mobile app makes a big point of having a nice soundtrack (but it's crap, so they failed on that point too).  If the business plan for a mobile app is to compete with Spotify, which is free and has effectively unlimited music, all of which is better than the music here, it's failed before it even started. Gamers can listen to the Spotify for free.  A game cannot be seen as recommendable just because it competes badly with listening to the radio or to MP3s.

Cosmophony didn't appeal much to the people who own a copy of the mobile app, either.  It has achievements, and they show us a very clear picture that the mobile app didn't really capture any interest from gamers.  The most commonly and easily attained achievement is for passing the first level, trivial to get, but less than 13 percent of players bothered to get that far before uninstalling the mobile app.  Hardly a success story, gamers just weren't all that interested in the mobile app.

Reviewing SteamDB to check how popular this mobile app was with players reveals a surprise... there's a very healthy spike in player counts for the mobile app.  But this isn't consistent with the achievement stats, that show less than 13 percent of players bothered playing the mobile app for any reasonable amount of time.  How is it possible for this mobile app to have so many concurrent players who weren't even playing the mobile app?  Trading cards.  Players will use card idling software to collect the cards and sell them, but this won't trigger any achievements in-game.  That tells us people only really bought this mobile app for trading cards, and that's a damning indictment of the woeful quality.  A closer look at the numbers shows the mobile app just has a couple of players every week running up the mobile app and idling it for cards, then deleting it.  We must ask how it benefits gamers for there to be so many games like this, with no merit as a serious game, that only generate sales from people idling and selling the trading cards.

Once more we see greedy mobile devs trying to scam PC gamers. On Steam, this is $5 USD, on app stores, it's free. Mobile devs must learn PC gamers are not here to be gouged, and can't be expected to pay a premium for a free mobile app just because it's been lazily dumped on Steam.  This is unacceptable disrespect for PC gamers.  Because this can be played free elsewhere, and because of the other defects, it's impossible to recommend.  Who do they think we are?

Cosmophony é um jogo de ritmo e ação desenvolvido pela Bento Studio. Nesta análise, vamos explorar os principais aspectos do jogo, incluindo jogabilidade, música, gráficos, pontos positivos e negativos, e o porquê de recomendar ou não.

Jogabilidade:
A jogabilidade de Cosmophony é baseada em ritmo e ação. Os jogadores controlam uma nave espacial e precisam navegar por diferentes ambientes, evitando obstáculos e inimigos, ao ritmo da música. Cada nível é sincronizado com uma trilha sonora eletrônica empolgante e desafiadora. A jogabilidade é rápida e requer reflexos rápidos, adicionando um elemento de intensidade à experiência.

Música:
A música é um dos pontos fortes de Cosmophony. Cada nível é acompanhado por uma trilha sonora eletrônica dinâmica, que se adapta à ação do jogo. A música aumenta a imersão e a emoção, criando uma experiência auditiva envolvente. A sincronização entre os obstáculos, a jogabilidade e a música é bem executada, proporcionando uma sensação satisfatória de progresso e ritmo.

Gráficos:
Os gráficos de Cosmophony são minimalistas e estilizados. O jogo utiliza uma paleta de cores vibrantes e efeitos visuais simples, mas eficazes, para transmitir uma sensação de velocidade e movimento. Embora não seja o ponto forte do jogo, os gráficos são agradáveis ​​e complementam bem a jogabilidade.

Pontos Positivos:

Jogabilidade viciante e desafiadora.
Trilha sonora eletrônica empolgante e sincronizada com a ação.
Atmosfera imersiva e emocionante.
Controles responsivos e intuitivos.
Duração dos níveis adequada para sessões de jogo rápidas.

Pontos Negativos:

Variedade limitada de mecânicas de jogabilidade.
Alguns jogadores podem achar a dificuldade elevada demais.

Por que recomendar:
Recomendo o jogo Cosmophony devido à sua jogabilidade viciante, trilha sonora eletrônica empolgante e atmosfera imersiva. O jogo oferece uma experiência de ritmo e ação desafiadora, que cativa os jogadores desde o início. A sincronização perfeita entre a música e a jogabilidade cria momentos emocionantes e satisfatórios. Embora a variedade de mecânicas de jogabilidade possa ser limitada, a jogabilidade rápida e os controles responsivos compensam esse aspecto. Cosmophony é uma ótima escolha para os fãs de jogos de ritmo e música eletrônica.

The levels are really well crafted, the flow of gameplay goes really nicely with the music. Gameplay in general feels amazing. Of all the rythm games I've played (osu!, ddr, cytus, audiosurf to name a few) this captures the feel of the music the absolute best by a LONG way. Being able to move with the music is spectacular.

The last level is a little challenging.
Depending on who you are and how many similar games you've played you may find all of it hard, or all of it easy.

I felt the music was good, it did what it needed to do, but that's a super subjective topic so your mileage may vary.

The models have some room for improvement, I get the devs were going for a minimalist vibe but the "block" asset definitely feels like a "programmer" asset. (Some beveling, normal maps, and shader work would have gone a long way and only takes a little while, many artists would do that for scraps, especially when you have only 1 real 3D asset and it's nearly a cube.)

Finally: the story was somewhat lacking. It's an abstract story about the guardian of the universe...kinda works with the music, but the game is very short and it lacks some fundamental elements like suspense, twists, and (for the most part) character interaction. The reason I'm giving them a pass on this is because the game doesn't focus on the story, and it never claims to. It's about the gameplay, which feels amazing.

If I were to describe this game, it would be the lovechild of Audiosurf and Geometry dash (although I don't own Audiosurf, I've seen gameplay videos of it). I got a coupon for this game and thought I'd try it to see how it was. 

It's not often a rhythm game feels as high-intensity as this does. With a spectacular Drum & Bass soundtrack (that's [i]free dlc[/i] as of writing this review) and three buttons to control the main gameplay, this game's easy to pick up and enjoy.

The gameplay strongly caters to moving and firing your 'ship' to the rhythm of the song; it's not very apparent in earlier levels, but after level 2, the fact that the levels are based off the rhythm are what make the otherwise impossible levels a playable, enjoyable challenge. One thing to note is that the game gets pretty hard pretty fast; then again, there are only 5 levels, so each level counts for 20% of progress. Of course the first 40% of the game would be easy; at level 4, naturally one would expect a game to become very difficult towards the end of the game. One thing I enjoyed about the game is that during each level, it's easy to ask "How can it get any harder than this?", only for your mind to be obliterated into tiny little bits when you reach the next level, especially after clearing level 4; I personally believe Stage 5 is preparing me for Dark Souls. To get a feel for just how hard the game gets, I looked at the global achievement stats; 7.3% of players have cleared level 4, and 2.9% of players have clared level 5 (as of writing this review).

As stated before, there are 5 levels, and 5 achievements; one achievement for clearing each level. And like Geometry dash, there's a practice mode (complete with checkpoints) so you can practice different sections of each stage to your hearts content before attempting to clear the level in one go. 

I paid just shy of $2 with a coupon, and as of right now I feel every penny was worth it. If you like rhythm-based fast-paced gameplay that's easy to pick up yet challenging, look no further than Cosmophony.

I kept going back and forth on this game, even considered giving up on the last level. But I've been enjoying it immensely the whole journey.
Because the video trailer is misleading (in a negative way) and tells you nothing about what [i]Cosmophony[/i] feels like, I encourage you to see [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=564193901]my gameplay video[/url] (no commentary). I hope you can understand how enjoyable it was to play the game in this manner.
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=564193901
The first two levels allow you to follow the tune to a great extent and can be perfected by anyone, and the game is totally worth it for that feeling alone. The following levels, though, made me feel confused. At first they just seemed like a bunch of random obstacles. But understanding came with time and practice. A big component in this game is memorization (yes, the levels are not generated; same every time). Usually I'm an opponent of memorization, but here it's very pleasant, because the levels are indeed tuned to the music. Knowing what comes next in the music is vital for knowing when to expect the obstacles. And the so called "muscle memory" helps with the obstacles themselves.

To complete a level (a bit under 2 minutes each) you need to go through it from the beginning to the end without failing. It's a bit annoying that the difficult parts are usually towards the end. But the game can't be blamed, because there is a practice mode with plenty of checkpoints and free traversal between them. For more casual gameplay you don't even have to play outside of the practice mode. Even so, the final levels can be a nightmare to complete if you don't get into the right mindset.

[i]Cosmophony[/i] is played mainly with 2 directional buttons which let you switch between the 7 lanes. Then there is the [i]shoot[/i] button which you should use whenever there is a special kind of obstacle in front of you. This mechanic is very simple and there is no penalty for spamming the button all the time, or just evading these obstacles. Even so, this mechanic is beneficial to the gameplay. If you want to make the game even more interesting, you can try to shoot to the beat instead of just spamming, like I did in my video. Destroying every destroyable obstacle is the requirement for "perfect" completion of each level, but it's not something that everyone should do (there aren't even achievements for this).

Another thing I would note is that, especially in the later levels, the music's rhythm sometimes corresponds to when the obstacles pass you, and not to when you need to move away, so you need to make a big mental effort to not press the keyboard button when you hear a beat, but instead anticipate it and move before it.

Graphics are nice and clean. Music is made by a great Drum&Bass artist [i]Salaryman[/i].

In conclusion, I really liked the game, but I realize that it may be just because I'm part of the target audience and because I worked around potential annoyances to make it interesting for myself, so can't give it a 10/10.

[h1]Overview[/h1]
[i]Cosmophony[/i] is a small rhythm game with five songs to play, where you control a small ship, and need to dodge incoming obstacles. The concept is simple, the controls even more so, but the difficulty curve is one of the most abrupt I've seen in rhythm games.

[h1]The Pros:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Good Music[/b] - The most important aspect of a music based games is, well, the music. It's a collection of five Drum&Bass songs by the same artist. There is sufficient diversity between them to entertain, and the melody is catchy too!

[*][b]Lovely Design[/b] - The game adopts a minimalist approach when it comes to graphics and UI, and damn, it looks good and makes it easier for your eyes to notice screen elements more easily. Here your reflexes are really important, and a good plain color contrast between obstacles and the road is welcomed. Minor shading is also present. The menus look very sleek and I like them too.

[*][b]Entangling Challenge[/b] - If you could pass each level on the first try, it would only require you 25 minutes of your time to complete the game. However, that can easily turn in quite the few hours because it is very challenging. But it's the good type of challenge - the kind that has you replay the level again and again because surely a stupid game isn't better than you. Come on, you can do it!

[*][b]Free OST[/b] - You can get the song files for free as a DLC. Be sure to get it from the app page.

[*][b]Achievements[/b] - There are only five: Complete level X. Which is great for achievement hunters... assuming you can complete the game.
[/list]

[h1]The Cons:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Insane Difficulty Curve[/b] - Level 1 is easy. Level 2 is a bit harder, but manageable. Level 3 requires a couple dozen tries to get accustomed to, Level 4 is... holy $#!^. Level 5... I haven't reached yet.
[/list]

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
You pay 5 bucks (coupons are fairly common, too) for five songs and a nice reflex game to encase them. Free OST, great deal, good if you have time (and nerves) to kill.

Quando estava para sair esse jogo eu olhei ali na lista e descobri que iria gostar bastante pelo nível de dificuldade! Estava tão anscioso que comprei pelo valor completo mesmo.

Cara imagina algo não tão difícil como "Super Hexagon", mas nem tão fácil como "The Impossible Game" (Ambos jogos completei 100% de conquistas). Bom, pensei comigo, vamos tentar já que de vez em quando preciso de algo difícil para me distrair com alguns assuntos pessoais. O quê descobri? Só ler abaixo...


Basicamente, o que no video e imagem você chamaria de "nave", seria o coração de uma deusa aprisionada no espaço. Seu objetivo é matá-la para libertar o espaço, ou pelo menos o que entendi.

Sabe o que é rídiculo? Um jogo desses ter história, o que achei estranho na primeira vez. Segundo, abro o jogo e começa a spawnar palavras em PT-BR? E depois eu vi que o jogo além de ter suporte para Português Brasileiro, tem para outras línguas, mas é algo tão mínimo para traduzir que seria a mesma coisa de falar que "A Bird Story" tem tradução para todas as línguas, quando todos nós sabemos que o jogo não tem nem palavra, mas ok! Voltando ao Cosmophony...

[b]Aqui você tem algumas opções interessantes![/b]

Você é o coração e precisa esquivar de "blocos do espaço" (Sim! É estranho, mas enfim..), vença o desafio e a Deusa irá te falar como liberar ela mesma e o espaço junto.

- Temos Modo Prática: Treine suas habilidades! Repita quantas vezes quiser e quando estiver pronto para o verdadeiro desafio, mude para modo normal.

- Temos Modo Normal: O verdadeiro desafio, destrua todos os inimigos (triângulos) e esquive de tudo sem morrer para completar e seguir ao seguinte level. Além de que existem várias animações para te distrair, então esteja realmente FOCADO no jogo, caso contrário, prepare-se para morrer DIVERSAS VEZES.

- Videos: Veja todo o video criado especialmente para aquela fase em específica no jogo.

[h1]*Músicas:[/h1]

As músicas foram feitas para ficar horas e horas num jogo sem cansar da mesma. Sabe as músicas de "Super Hexagon" e "The Impossible Game"? Você ouve, ouve e não enjoa? Justamente isso que falo daqui...

[h1]*Jogabilidade:[/h1]

Como qualquer nave que segue um caminho seu espaço é limitado, você pode ir só para direita e esquerda e atirar para destruir seus inimigos. O jogo diz que combina música com jogabilidade, porém... não é bem assim, muitas das vezes você atira antes de efeito de som ser reproduzido e com essa dessincronização que é um pouco rara, você percebe que seu tiro não tem efeito nenhum de som o que fica meio decepcionante, mas isso é apenas uma observação que não deve ser levada muito em conta.

*Opinião Pessoal:

Fase treinamento: Normal é um treinamento, então irá te mostrar o que você deve destruir, e o que deve esquivar.

Fase 1: Não tão difícil, mas é o começo da dificuldade muitas vezes!

Fase 2: Melhor música! Mas em questão de fase é algo para aprender a FOCAR no jogo e não distrai-se, distração seja de alguém te chamando, seja da própria Steam é algo que o jogo não tolera. Recomendo se tiver muitos amigos para falar, desativar o Steam Overlay do jogo ou as mensagens em si, se tiver problemas de concentração.

Fase 3: O que posso dizer? Eu passei de primeira no modo normal, mas fiquei treinando no modo prática durante um certo tempo também.

Fase 4: Aqui O jogo quer te mostrar que você precisa lembrar, prestar atenção, focar e ser perfeito, só assim será possível passar essa fase. Uma vez vencido Fase 4, você nunca mais esquece a combinação das coisas

Fase 5: "O verdadeiro Desafio", eu cheguei na fase 5 no primeiro dia de jogo sem problemas, mas passar isso aqui é algo tão desumano que é comparado com o nível hardtestest do "Super Hexagon" (Modo mais difícil do jogo, preto e branco)... Aqui existe tanta coisa para esquivar, como para ser rápido no botão que meu deus.... Vai demorar um pouco, mas não é algo complicado... É só lembrar das combinações e ser habilidoso nas teclas! E digo MUITO HABILIDOSO.


[h1]Comentários Finais:[/h1]

O próprio jogo diz, "feito para pessoas experimentadas, cada fase tem um certo nível alto de dificuldade, mas proporciona uma grande experiência única". E realmente é isso mesmo.

Cosmophony is, in general, quite a fun rythmic shooter. I actually found myself needing to use the music to manuever throughout the levels! There are 5 levels, split into 10 sections each which you can practice individually in the practice mode.
Graphically, this game at first gave me a bad impression, but then i ignored the graphics and started to see through to the gameplay.
My biggest complaint about this game is that the level can launch things at you so quickly that it almost seems unfair the first few times you play. It could call itself fair by saying that you could get past these obstacles with ninja-like reflexes, but it still is something that will make you rage. There's also quite a difficulty spike once you get to level 4. I found myself beating the first 3 levels in an hour, and then that level took me about 1.5 hours (I still have not beaten level 5).

While I enjoy it, I feel like a lot of the difficulty comes from memorization more than actually being a difficult reaction/precision game. Mechanics change mid level with no time to react, targets are hidden and require specific movement to setup a way to reach them. (Trying not to spoil anything) On the fifth level the timing of the gimmick mechanic seems really dodgy one moment and fine the next. I know where I'm supposed to be positioned at what time, but its hit or miss if the game reacts like I expect it to. Might be better if there wasn't any delay between key presses and lane switching but theres a small delay that is easily noticable when trying to quickly move from one side of the screen to the other. Makes hitting some of the timing goals a lot harder than they need to be.

That being said its cheap, the music is good, and its definitely an interesting game. If it ever goes on sale I couldn't recommend it more. But 5.50 CAD is probably the upper limit on what I'd spend on 5 levels with no level editor. (User generated content would be amazing, and if that ever happens, I'll be buying a copy of this for all my friends :p)

This is probably one of my favorite hidden gems of all time.

An incredibly cool and difficult game that frequently stunned me from how purely epic it is, despite only having five levels.  Rez fans, this is your challenge—Cosmophony is a mind-blowing package of smart art, music, sound, and level design.  Also just like Rez, I find myself replaying beaten levels for the sheer joy of it, even almost a decade later.

Its merciless difficulty gives you a real sense of accomplishment, the game exploding to celebrate how freaking badass you are for passing its challenges.  If Sid Meier's Civilization embodies "one more turn", Cosmophony is "one more try".  Memorization can be a dirty word in games, but Cosmophony turns trial-and-error into a dance worth learning.

[h1]On bouge sur 7 lignes, on tir, on évite les obstacles... on meurt et on recommence. D&B power![/h1]

Voyez le [b]plus comme un jeu de mémorisation avec une grande emphase sur la musique;[/b] Cosmophony est un titre héritier de l'école du parcoeurisme: on pratique un tantinet en mode entrainement, on s'entraine, on s'entraine... et puis quand on se sent prêt, on éssaye de terminer le titre en mode normal avec comme objectif "zéro fautes" sinon, on recommence depuis le début!
Dès le second stage, on s'attaque à un mur, qui va vous imposer cette pratique: [b]vous devez réussir les stages en normal(perfect stage donc) pour débloquer les suivants.[/b]

Vous pouvez voir çà comme une manière de rajouter de la durée de vie artificiellement, ou le voir comme un titre qui assume son côté [b]exigeant[/b] et s'adressant à un public de perfectionnistes(la seconde pour moi, car j'en ai bouffé de ce type de jeux :P).

La bande son du titre est composés exclusivement de [b]Drum&Bass/techstep;[/b] implique un tempo de base très rapide et pas mal de variation rythmiques qui se traduisent en patterns diverses ingame. Votre attrait pour ce genre de musique va y être pour beaucoup dans celui que vous allez avoir pour le jeu, car si on ne vous demande pas que les tirs et mouvement de votre vaisseau soient exactement en symbiose avec le rythme, ce dernier est directer lié aux obstacles que vous allez rencontré(comme "Audiosurf", quoi!).

Le jeu assume aussi son côté psychédélique avec une histoire d'entité virtuelle à sauver("Rez" est tu là?^^) et un visuel minimaliste.

Pour toute personne qui connait la série des "Bit Trip"(runner, beat etc...) et "Audiosurf", le jeu ne surprendra personne...  mais pour tous ceux qui n'ont rien contre un peu de challenge(du type des masochistes de "Super Hexagon"), il vaut le prix demandé.

Bonne pioche!
